questions.question_text: A horizontal line and a vertical line are extended until they meet. What must be true?

options.why: Confuses two different compass directions with lines running in the same direction.
Uses a straight-angle value instead of the right angle between horizontal and vertical.
Misses that horizontal and vertical directions always form a right angle.

questions.solution_text:
Horizontal and vertical directions form a $90^{\circ}$ angle.
The lines are perpendicular.

questions.question_text: Given $r \perp s$ and $s \perp t$, which conclusion is correct?

options.why: Chains the perpendicular symbols as though perpendicularity were transitive.
Treats line relationships as an equality of the line names.
Halves a right angle without any geometric reason.

questions.solution_text:
Both $r$ and $t$ make a $90^{\circ}$ angle with $s$.
Therefore $r$ and $t$ run in the same direction, so $r \parallel t$.
